kicker: Mist clears from a whole stack of frames, all at once.
summary: Video AI denoises a whole block of frames at once; staying consistent is hard, and it’s very costly.

quiz.q: To keep a character identical across many clips, what’s the surest way?
options: Write a very long, detailed prompt
Make one very long video in one go
quiz.explain: An approved image already locks in the face, outfit and product; AI only needs to add motion.

block.label: A block of time
block.art: A stack of see-through frames lined up in time, all grainy noise at first. Drag and the frames clear together into a scene of egrets flying over a lake at dawn.
block.noWebgl: This browser can’t show the 3D scene yet.
block.insight: Video AI denoises a whole block of frames at once, so the frames line up into smooth motion.

detail.text: Like image AI, but with time added: every second holds dozens of frames, so making video usually takes far more computing than images or text.

glitch.insight: A video is many frames that must match; staying consistent over time is hard, so objects, hands and text easily go wrong.
glitch.detail: Good habit: keep clips short, one action per clip; check hands, text and logos closely; if something’s off, regenerate.

concepts.label: Seven ways to steer

items.name: Text → video
items.caption: Type one description; AI builds a whole clip out of a mist of noise.
words: “A white egret over the lake at dawn”

items.name: Image → video
items.caption: Start from an approved image: the surest way to keep characters and products consistent.

items.name: First – last frame
items.caption: Give AI the first and last frames; it draws the motion in between.

items.name: Camera
items.caption: Direct the camera: pan, push in, pull out.

items.name: Native audio
items.caption: Dialogue, sound effects and music are generated with the picture, in sync.

items.name: Length limit
items.caption: Each generation makes only a short clip; long videos are many clips joined together.

items.name: Motion reference
items.caption: Give a sample clip; your character repeats exactly that movement.

concepts.insight: Each stone is one way to “steer” video AI; starting from an approved image is the steadiest.
concepts.detail: Good habit: start from an approved image, then add camera moves and sound; change only one thing at a time.

models.label: Standout models
models.needsGroup: What kind of video do you need?

insight.text: There’s no “best” video model: choose by the job — people in motion, sound, camera, or open weights.

models.detail: “Open weights”: anyone can download the model and run it on their own machine. Models change weekly, so try a few with the same prompt.

prompt.label: Writing video prompts
prompt.screen: A paper screen showing the clip being built: a wooden bridge over a misty lake; each prompt part you add changes the scene.
prompt.group: Five parts of a video prompt

parts.name: Subject
parts.words: A girl in a conical hat

prompt.rule: One scene · one action · short clip
prompt.insight: A good video prompt covers it all: who, doing what, how the camera moves, light, sound — one scene per clip.
prompt.detail: Write it like a director briefing the camera operator. For a long video, make it scene by scene and join them; change one part at a time to see its effect.

sora.label: The Sora story
sora.art: A paper screen named Sora in a night garden, with a row of small lanterns beside it — the apps that use Sora. Drag through 2026 to watch them go out one by one.

fact.text: Apr 26, 2026: OpenAI shut down the Sora app.
Sep 24, 2026: OpenAI also shut down the API, the gateway other software used to reach Sora.

reasonFact.text: Main reasons: far too costly to run, plus copyright and deepfake (fake videos of real people) problems.

insight.text: The lesson: video AI is very costly to run and brings real legal problems with it.

sora.detail: Good habit: make videos only when needed; don’t use real people’s faces or voices without permission; clearly label AI-made content.
